title: Design-traced anomalies (any scenario)
assumptions: Design anomalies fire only when the engineering analysis already flags the matching constraint (data return / link margin, battery reserve / energy closure, pointing, delta-v margin): the run tells the same story as the analysis, and a design the analysis clears sees none of them (no random punishment).
severityThreshold values only choose warning vs critical (gameplay-estimate); effect sizes are gameplay-estimate teaching values, not flight rules.

anomalies.title: Missed contact: data backlog
anomalies.situation: The ground station loses lock during a pass and the planned contact is missed; with no slack in the downlink plan the collected data stays on board and a data backlog builds up.
anomalies.prompt: How should operations respond to the fading link?
anomalies.counterfactual: Give the downlink plan slack (more or longer contacts, a higher-gain radio or a lower planned data volume) so the analysis data-return and link-margin checks pass and one lost pass does not leave data on board.

choices.label: Halve the downlink rate
choices.tradeoff: About 3 dB more link margin for the rest of the mission, but each pass returns half the data, so the backlog drains slowly.

choices.label: Keep the planned rate
choices.tradeoff: Full-rate passes once the link recovers, but the marginal link keeps dropping passes for the next 6 days and the backlog grows.

anomalies.title: Power low during science
anomalies.situation: The battery approaches its reserve floor while the instruments draw science power.
anomalies.counterfactual: Size the arrays and battery so the analysis battery-reserve and energy-closure checks pass.

choices.label: Shed instrument load
choices.tradeoff: The battery recovers, but observations in the next 3 days are not flown.

choices.label: Keep observing
choices.tradeoff: No science time lost, but the battery drops a further 25 % of capacity; if it empties the spacecraft is lost.

anomalies.title: Pointing drift
anomalies.situation: Attitude errors drift towards the instrument pointing requirement during the first observation.
anomalies.prompt: Recalibrate the attitude system or keep observing?
anomalies.counterfactual: Choose an ADCS whose accuracy meets the tightest instrument pointing requirement, so the analysis credits the pointing.

choices.label: Recalibrate attitude control
choices.tradeoff: Sharper pointing afterwards, but observations in the next 2 days are not flown.

choices.label: Keep observing
choices.tradeoff: No science time lost, but 30 % of the buffered data is smeared and discarded.

anomalies.title: Correction-maneuver shortfall
anomalies.situation: Navigation asks for a trajectory correction, but the propellant headroom above the planned maneuvers is thin.
anomalies.prompt: Spend the reserve, skip the correction, or end the mission?
anomalies.counterfactual: Keep a positive delta-v margin after the planned maneuvers and reserve (more propellant or a higher-Isp system), so the analysis delta-v check passes.

choices.label: Burn the reserve
choices.tradeoff: The correction is flown on time, using 15 % of the loaded propellant.

choices.label: Skip the correction
choices.tradeoff: Propellant is kept, but the arrival dispersion costs 15 days of observations while the target is re-acquired.

choices.label: End the mission
choices.tradeoff: The spacecraft is safed and the mission ends now; the postmortem explains what the design lacked.
